tasks.short: Listen in order to master the piece.

steps.what: Queue the recording the musician has already chosen.
Listen to recordings to master pieces or to maintain and improve skills.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store queues a recording only when the musician has already chosen it. The musician listens, to master the piece or to maintain and improve the skill. The queue does not listen and does not recommend another recording. A missing choice leaves the queue empty.
tasks.previous_blocker: The recording was a file with a vague name, and the musician hunted for the take before listening.
tasks.enabler_now: A chosen recording can be queued. The listening stays with the musician.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what still needs work in a piece takes the musician's ear, not a queue.
tasks.human_edge: The musician listens and judges the piece. The queue only opens the file already chosen.
tasks.altitude: Listening stays with the musician. Nothing is recommended, and only a recording the musician already chose is queued.

reach.task: Watch a tape of their own scene to hear what to fix.
reach.learn: Opening the file is not the watching.

evidence.claim: Queuing a recording the musician already chose opens a file. It does not listen, and it does not master the piece.
Recommending a different recording would be a new choice. This task does not make one.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A musician or singer in a mid-size European company. A score on screen is not a performance, and a draft note is not the research.
Fields: The recording id the musician already chose. A blank choice does not pick a file. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the musician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Play the file from the document store already used for recordings.
unknowns: Whether the recordings are the musician's own takes or reference performances.
research_questions: Who is allowed to hear a take that includes other performers?

already_counted.description: Listening to master the piece stays with the musician.

incremental.description: Remove queued files when the musician drops that piece.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The musician still listens in order to master the piece or keep the skill. Only queuing a recording already chosen is removed. No recommendation is made, and a week with no chosen file saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the slate already written for this recording session.
Make or participate in the recording.
Keep or discard the take after hearing the recording.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the slate already written for the session. The musician makes the recording or participates in it, then keeps or discards the take after hearing it. The slate does not record the take. A session with no slate leaves the screen blank. The decision is the musician's ear, not a label.
tasks.previous_blocker: The slate was spoken at the top of the take, and a bad take was kept because the note was lost.
tasks.enabler_now: A written slate can be shown. Performing the take and keeping it stay with the musician.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing whether a take is the one to keep takes the musician after the red light.
tasks.human_edge: The musician performs the take and keeps or discards it after hearing it.
tasks.altitude: The recording stays with the musician. The slate is a label already written, and the keep-or-discard decision is unchanged.

reach.task: Run the machine while the musician makes the take.
reach.learn: The slate is not the musical take.

evidence.claim: A slate already written labels the take. It does not make the recording or decide that the take is kept.
Keeping a take is the musician's judgement after hearing it. The slate has no opinion of the performance.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A musician or singer in a mid-size European company. A score on screen is not a performance, and a draft note is not the research.
Fields: The session id and the slate only if it is already written. The slate is not generated from the audio. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the musician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the slate from the document store already used for the session.
unknowns: Whether the musician or a producer has the last word on keeping a take.
research_questions: Which takes must be heard in full before they are kept?

already_counted.description: Making the recording and keeping the take stay with the musician.

incremental.description: Drop slates for sessions that were cancelled.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The musician still makes or participates in the recording and still keeps or discards the take after hearing it. Only showing a slate already written is removed. A session with no slate saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the studio booking and the microphone plot already drawn.
Make or participate in recordings in music studios.
Move a microphone the plot got wrong for the room.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} shows the studio booking and the microphone plot if one is already drawn. The musician records in the music studio. A microphone the plot got wrong for the room is moved by the musician. The plot does not record the take. A booking with no plot leaves that line blank, and the musician places the microphone by ear.
tasks.previous_blocker: The studio time was a mail, and the microphone plot was a sketch that did not match the room.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking and a stored plot can be shown. Recording in the room, and moving a wrong microphone, stay physical.
tasks.still_hard: A plot can name a place that sounds wrong once the musician is in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The musician records in the studio and moves a microphone the room does not support.
tasks.altitude: Studio recording stays in the room. The booking and the plot are visible, and a wrong microphone is still moved by the musician.

reach.task: Place a microphone and then move it when the room disagrees.
reach.learn: The plot is not the sound in the room.

evidence.claim: A studio booking and a stored microphone plot are records. They do not make the recording.
Moving a microphone is the musician's decision after hearing the room. The plot cannot hear it.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A musician or singer in a mid-size European company. A score on screen is not a performance, and a draft note is not the research.
Fields: The booking id and the plot only if it is already drawn. The plot is not generated. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the musician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the booking from the calendar already used for the studio.
unknowns: Whether an engineer, rather than the musician, owns the microphone plot.
research_questions: Who may change the plot once the session has started?

already_counted.description: Recording in the studio and moving a microphone stay with the musician.

incremental.description: Update the plot when a microphone position is kept for the next session.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The musician still records in the music studio and still moves a microphone the room does not support. Only showing a booking and a plot already drawn is removed. A session with no plot saves nothing of the recording.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sing the solo or the ensemble part.

steps.what: Show whether the programme lists this singer as soloist or as a member.
Sing as a soloist or as a member of a vocal group.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows whether the programme already lists the singer as soloist or as a member of the vocal group. The musician sings that part. The listing does not sing. A programme that does not say which leaves the screen blank, and the singer takes the part the conductor gives in the room. No voice is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Solo and ensemble were a handwritten programme, and a wrong part was started.
tasks.enabler_now: The programme line can be shown. Singing the part stays with the musician.
tasks.still_hard: Blend, pitch, and the solo line itself take the singer, not a label on the programme.
tasks.human_edge: The musician sings. The programme only says soloist or member, and only if it already says so.
tasks.altitude: Singing stays in the musician's voice. The programme label is visible, and no voice is generated.

reach.task: Speak a solo line or a line inside a crowd scene.
reach.learn: The cast list does not speak.

evidence.claim: A programme line that already says soloist or member is a label. It does not sing the part.
No voice is generated. The part is sung by the musician.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A musician or singer in a mid-size European company. A score on screen is not a performance, and a draft note is not the research.

Fields: The programme id and the soloist or member flag only if the programme already has it. The flag is not inferred. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the musician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the programme from the document store. Do not add a voice tool.
unknowns: Whether one singer is listed as both soloist and ensemble member in the same programme.
research_questions: Who changes the soloist line after the programme is printed?

already_counted.description: Singing the part stays with the musician.

incremental.description: Correct the soloist flag when the programme is reprinted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The musician still sings as soloist or as a member of the vocal group. Only showing a flag already printed on the programme is removed. No voice is generated, and a programme without the flag saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The musician still listens, still records, and still sings. A slate or a studio booking can be shown. The take and the voice stay with the musician.
reach: Audio and video technicians run a session, and this job learns the musical take is the musician's.
Actors record a voice, and this job learns the studio booking is not the performance.
skills_to_grow: Listen to the recording in order to master the piece.
Keep or discard a take only after hearing it.
Sing the solo or the ensemble part in the musician's own voice.
role.ambitious_version: Listening, session takes, studio recording, and singing stay with the musician. Bookings and slates only show what was already written.
